content:
# Testament of Issachar — 5
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

1:1 A-copy-of-the-words of-Issachar, the-fifth-son of-Jacob and-Leah.
1:2 For-he-called-his-sons-together and-said-to-them:
1:3 Hearken, my-children, to-Issachar your-father; give-heed-to-the-words-of-him-who-is-beloved-of-the-LORD.
1:4 I-was-born the-fifth-to-Jacob, for-a-reward for-the-mandrakes.
1:5 For-Reuben my-brother brought-in-mandrakes-from-the-field, and-Rachel-met-him-and-took-them.
1:6 And-Reuben-wept, and-Leah my-mother came-out and-said-to-her: Wilt-thou-take-also-the-husband-of-my-youth?
1:7 And-Rachel said-to-her: Let-him-be-thine-this-night-for-thy-son's-mandrakes.
1:8 And-Jacob knew-Leah, and-she-conceived-and-bore-me, and-she-called-my-name Issachar, because-of-the-reward.

2:1 And-then-came-an-angel-of-the-LORD to-Leah, and-said: Two-children-shalt-thou-yet-bear, for-thou-hast-given-to-thy-sister-thy-husband's-mandrakes, and-thy-modesty-pleases-God.
2:2 And-the-angel-of-the-LORD appeared-also-to-Rachel, and-told-her that-she-should-not-be-fruitless-for-ever; for-she-should-conceive-two-children, but-they-should-be-born-later than-all-the-children-of-Leah.
2:3 And-she-gave-up-the-mandrakes-for-the-sake-of-children-according-to-the-word-of-the-angel-of-the-LORD.

3:1 For-I-was-a-simple-man and-I-tilled-the-ground, and-I-brought-forth-fruits-of-the-field for-my-father Jacob; and-my-father loved-me, for-my-simplicity.
3:2 And with-the-fruit-of-my-labour I-enriched-my-father; and I-also-gave-to-the-poor-of-the-land.
3:3 And-I-ate-of-the-good-things-of-the-earth only, and-I-had-no-wickedness-in-me.
3:4 I-knew-not-of-any-sin-in-myself; my-days-were-consumed-in-simplicity.
3:5 And-I-had-no-double-mind towards-any-man, and-no-hatred-in-my-heart toward-any-man; I-was-always-in-singleness-of-heart.

4:1 I-loved-the-LORD with-all-my-strength; likewise-also-I-loved-every-man-as-I-love-my-children.
4:2 Do-ye-also-these-things, my-children, and-every-spirit-of-Beliar-will-flee-from-you, and-no-deed-of-wicked-men-will-have-dominion-over-you; and-every-wild-beast-will-ye-subdue, since-ye-have-with-you-the-God-of-heaven-and-earth and-walk-with-men-in-singleness-of-heart.
4:3 Guard-therefore simplicity, my-children, and-walk-in-singleness-of-heart, not-prying-into-the-affairs-of-your-neighbour; but-love-the-LORD and-love-your-neighbour; pity-the-poor-and-the-weak.
4:4 Bow-your-back in-husbandry, and-labour in-all-manner-of-works-of-the-earth, offering-gifts-to-the-LORD in-thankfulness.
4:5 For-with-the-first-fruits-of-the-earth-will-the-LORD-bless-you, even-as-he-blessed-all-the-saints-from-Abel-even-unto-this-day.
4:6 For-no-other-thing-was-given-to-you-save-that-of-the-fruit-of-the-earth-for-an-inheritance.

5:1 Know-ye-therefore, my-children, that-in-the-last-times your-sons-will-forsake-simplicity, and-will-cleave-to-insatiable-desire; and-leaving-behind-guilelessness-will-draw-near-to-malice; and-forsaking-the-commandments-of-the-LORD, they-will-cleave-to-Beliar.
5:2 And-they-will-leave-husbandry, and-will-follow-after-their-own-wicked-devices, and-will-be-dispersed-among-the-nations, and-will-serve-their-enemies.
5:3 Tell-ye-therefore-these-things-to-your-children, that, if-they-sin, they-may-the-more-quickly-return-to-the-LORD.
5:4 For-he-is-merciful, and-will-deliver-them, and-will-bring-them-back-into-their-land.

6:1 And-behold I-am-a-hundred-and-twenty-six-years-old and-I-perceive-in-me-no-sin.
6:2 Except-my-wife I-have-not-known-any-woman; I-have-not-committed-fornication-by-the-uplifting-of-my-eyes.
6:3 I-drank-not-wine, to-be-led-astray-thereby; I-coveted-not-any-desirable-thing-that-was-my-neighbour's.
6:4 Guile-arose-not-in-my-heart; a-lie-passed-not-through-my-lips.
6:5 If-any-man-were-in-distress-I-joined-my-sighs-with-his, and I-shared-my-bread-with-the-poor.
6:6 I-wrought-godliness-all-my-days-and-truth.
6:7 I-loved-the-LORD; likewise-also-every-man-with-all-my-heart.
6:8 So-do-ye-also-these-things, my-children, and-every-spirit-of-Beliar-shall-flee-from-you.

7:1 And-when-he-had-said-these-things, he-commanded-his-sons that-they-should-carry-him-up-to-Hebron, and-bury-him-there-with-his-fathers.
7:2 And-he-stretched-out-his-feet and-fell-asleep-in-peace.
7:3 And-after-five-years-his-sons-carried-him-up to-Hebron and-buried-him-with-his-fathers.

---
*End of Testament of Issachar*
